issues.legal_issue: A limitation objection is an objection to jurisdiction that must be tried as a preliminary issue when raised at the hearing of an application for interim relief in a suit governed by the state-amended procedure.
material_facts: The appeals concerned civil suits in which applications for interim relief were pending and defendants raised objections to the suits’ maintainability, including objections based on limitation.
In the principal suit, the plaintiff relied on an earlier suit and sought the benefit of time spent pursuing it; the defendants argued that the suit was time-barred.

The courts below treated limitation as a preliminary issue and dismissed the principal suit as time-barred, while other appeals challenged whether limitation could be considered at the preliminary stage.
issues.conclusion: Limitation falls within the jurisdiction objection covered by the state-amended procedure. When that procedure applies and a limitation objection is raised at the hearing of an interim-relief application, the court must determine the objection as a preliminary issue before deciding whether to grant or set aside interim relief. The provision is mandatory and prevails over the ordinary procedure for deciding issues.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9A of the Code of Civil Procedure, as re-enacted by the Maharashtra amendment with presidential assent under Article 254(2) of the Constitution, creates a mandatory, self-contained procedure that overrides Order XIV Rule 2 when its conditions apply. Section 3 of the Limitation Act requires a time-barred suit to be dismissed, and a limitation plea is a plea of law concerning jurisdiction: Pandurang Dhondi Chougule v. Maruti Hari Jadhav; Manick Chandra Nandy v. Debdas Nandy; National Thermal Power Corpn. Ltd. v. Siemens Atkeingesellschaft; Official Trustee v. Sachindra Nath Chatterjee; ITW Signode India Ltd. v. CCE; and Kamlesh Babu v. Lajpat Rai Sharma. Ramesh B. Desai v. Bipin Vadilal Mehta concerned the ordinary procedure under Order XIV Rule 2 and did not govern the distinct state-amended procedure. The contrary view in Kamalakar Eknath Salunkhe v. Baburav Vishnu Javalkar was inconsistent with the binding larger-bench authorities.

predicates.state_amended_procedure_applies: The civil suit is governed by a state-amended procedure requiring an objection to the court’s jurisdiction to be decided at the interim-relief stage.
predicates.civil_suit_with_interim_relief_applicati: A party to a civil suit has sought interim relief and the court is hearing that application.
predicates.limitation_bar_pleaded: A party has objected that the suit is barred by limitation.

issues.definition: When a suit governed by the special state procedure is at the interim-relief stage and a party pleads a limitation bar, the court must decide that objection as a preliminary issue.

issues.legal_issue: Under the ordinary procedure, a court may try a qualifying issue of law first when it relates to jurisdiction or a legal bar and can dispose of the case or part of it.
material_facts: The parties disputed whether the special procedure for deciding jurisdiction objections at the interim-relief stage displaced the ordinary procedure for deciding preliminary issues.

The Court distinguished the ordinary procedure from the mandatory state-amended procedure and explained that the ordinary procedure leaves the decision to try an issue first to the court’s discretion.
issues.conclusion: In cases governed by the ordinary procedure, the court has discretion to try an issue of law first if the case or part of it may be disposed of on that issue and the issue relates to jurisdiction or a legal bar; it is not required to do so.
issues.legal_principle: Order XIV Rule 2(1) generally requires judgment on all issues. Under Order XIV Rule 2(2), the court may try first an issue of law that can dispose of the case or part of it and concerns jurisdiction or a bar created by law. Ramesh B. Desai v. Bipin Vadilal Mehta explains the treatment of limitation under that ordinary procedure. This discretion does not displace the mandatory state-amended procedure where that procedure applies.

predicates.ordinary_procedure_civil_suit: The case is a civil suit governed by the ordinary procedure rather than a special state-amended preliminary-issue procedure.
predicates.issue_of_law_can_dispose_case_or_part: The issue of law could dispose of the case or a part of it.
predicates.issue_concerns_jurisdiction_or_legal_bar: The issue of law concerns the court’s jurisdiction or a legal bar to the suit.

issues.definition: In an ordinary civil suit, the court may try an issue first when it could dispose of the case or part of it and concerns jurisdiction or a legal bar.
